summary:
Project Summary – **Cosmic Footprints** is an interactive, offline-ready educational website that explores NASA spacecraft and scientific equipment left on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space. We developed a visually engaging, space-themed timeline featuring seven missions: Surveyor 3, Apollo 11 Laser Reflector, Pioneer 10, Voyager 1 and 2, Opportunity, InSight, and Perseverance.

The website presents each mission through images, simplified explanations, current mission status, and important historical milestones. Users can navigate through missions using an interactive chronological timeline, with additional features such as scroll-based navigation, reading progress indicators, and subtle animations.

The project addresses the challenge of making complex space exploration history accessible and interesting, especially for students and young space enthusiasts. By combining reliable NASA information with an engaging and easy-to-navigate interface, Cosmic Footprints transforms scientific information into an interactive learning experience.

This project is important because it promotes scientific curiosity, improves awareness of space exploration, and helps users understand how past and ongoing NASA missions contribute to our knowledge of the universe.
details:
Project Details – Cosmic Footprints

Cosmic Footprints is an interactive, offline-ready educational website that explores seven NASA machines sent to the Moon, Mars and deep space. The project aims to make space exploration history interesting, accessible and easy to understand for students and space enthusiasts.

The website features an interactive chronological timeline covering Surveyor 3, Apollo 11 Laser Reflector, Pioneer 10, Voyager 1 and 2, Opportunity, InSight and Perseverance. Users can select different timeline stops to explore individual missions, view images, read simplified scientific explanations, understand mission milestones and discover the current status and location of each spacecraft.

Technologies Used: The website was developed using HTML5 for structure, CSS3 for styling, and JavaScript for interactive functionality. Node.js was used for the optional local development server, and Netlify was used to deploy the website publicly. NASA mission information and images were used as educational references.

Creative Features: The project includes a space-inspired visual design, interactive timeline navigation, animated scroll reveals, reading-progress indicators, responsive layouts and support for reduced-motion accessibility settings.

Impact: Cosmic Footprints transforms complex space exploration information into an engaging visual learning experience. It encourages scientific curiosity, promotes awareness of NASA missions and helps users appreciate the achievements of robotic space exploration. The project is designed to work without an internet connection once its files are available locally.
